name: Jamie

verdictSummary: The visible bot-free meeting notes loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Jamie earns its keep through capture, integrations, reliability, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private bot-free meeting notes pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: local Whisper model or optional API key in .env
whatYouLose: recording recovery, mastering, hosting, and distribution
whyPeopleStillPay: Jamie: Customers pay for automatic capture, dependable speaker handling, search across calls, and notes arriving without manual file wrangling.
ongoingBurden: Own audio capture permissions, diarization quality, model downloads, storage, privacy, and integrations.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local speech-to-text engine suitable for private transcription.

alternatives.name: Anarlog
alternatives.desc: A Mac meeting notepad with local transcripts, local files and bring-your-own summaries.

facts.install: Native desktop download; building and self-hosting from source are also supported
facts.engines: On-device transcription on supported Apple Silicon Macs; BYOK or hosted speech-to-text; OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, or another OpenAI-compatible LLM for summaries and chat
facts.dataFormat: Canonical meetings, notes and transcripts live in a local SQLite database and recordings/attachments are local files; Markdown export is available, with optional end-to-end-encrypted CloudSync and a separate opt-in server-readable Cloud API copy
facts.gapVsPaid: It can keep transcripts local, but local transcription is Apple-silicon-only and its younger product lacks Jamie's polished cross-platform managed meeting history and integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: Local transcription is limited to supported Apple Silicon Macs; other systems need hosted/BYOK transcription, while fully local summaries require installing and configuring Ollama or LM Studio

alternatives.name: Meetily
alternatives.desc: A local recorder and summarizer for Mac and Windows; no account, no meeting bot.

facts.install: Signed Windows x64 installer or Apple-silicon macOS DMG; Linux currently requires a source build
facts.engines: Local Whisper or NVIDIA Parakeet for transcription; local Ollama or the built-in summarizer, with Claude, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter and custom OpenAI-compatible summary providers depending on edition
facts.dataFormat: Transcription models, recordings, transcripts and application data stay on the local machine; the Community Edition has no cloud sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It avoids a bot and keeps data local, but the free Community Edition omits several advanced templates, exports and speaker workflows and has less seamless cross-device history than Jamie.
facts.setupBlocker: Windows and Apple-silicon macOS install cleanly but still need audio permissions and model downloads; Linux requires Rust/Node source-build tooling, and several advanced summary/export/diarization workflows are Pro-only

alternatives.name: Meeting Transcriber
alternatives.desc: A Mac menu-bar app that captures the call and emits decisions, tasks and a transcript as Markdown.

facts.install: Third-party Homebrew cask on macOS; source build is also supported
facts.engines: WhisperKit or NVIDIA Parakeet TDT v3 for local ASR; FluidAudio/CoreML for diarization, Silero v6 for VAD; Claude Code CLI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama, LM Studio, or llama.cpp for notes
facts.dataFormat: Local dual-track audio and optional JSON metadata in the configured output folder; raw transcripts as TXT and structured protocols as Markdown under ~/Library/Application Support/MeetingTranscriber/protocols by default, with voice embeddings and settings kept locally
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Mac-only and writes files rather than providing Jamie's managed cross-platform archive, integrations and frictionless meeting follow-up.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires macOS 14.2+, a third-party Homebrew tap trust step, microphone/accessibility permissions, first-run model downloads, and a Claude CLI login or local/API LLM if you want generated notes

alternatives.name: Muesli
alternatives.desc: Local mic-and-system capture, live transcription, summaries and action items in a signed Mac app.

facts.install: Signed macOS DMG or Homebrew cask
facts.engines: Parakeet TDT, Nemotron 3.5, Cohere Transcribe, Qwen3 ASR, SenseVoice, IndicConformer, experimental Gemma ASR, or WhisperKit locally; Silero VAD and FluidAudio/pyannote diarization; OpenAI, OpenRouter, ChatGPT OAuth, Ollama, LM Studio, or a custom LLM for notes
facts.dataFormat: Meeting history, transcripts, notes and settings live in a local SQLite database at ~/Library/Application Support/Muesli/muesli.db; captured audio and app-support files remain on the Mac, with optional text-only iCloud/CloudKit sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a strong signed Mac app, but Apple-silicon-only and less suitable than Jamie for mixed-device teams, managed synchronization and shared administrative workflows.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2+, microphone/accessibility/system-audio permissions, and a first model download; cloud summaries need an account or API key unless you configure Ollama or LM Studio

alternatives.name: OpenWhispr
alternatives.desc: Bot-free meeting capture, speaker labels and searchable notes in one cross-platform installer.

facts.install: Native DMG, EXE, AppImage, DEB or RPM; optional OpenWhispr Cloud account
facts.engines: Local Whisper/whisper.cpp or NVIDIA Parakeet via sherpa-onnx; local llama.cpp models or cloud/BYOK providers including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Tinfoil and OpenRouter
facts.dataFormat: Transcriptions and notes live in a local SQLite database; optional retained audio stays on-device, and optional Cloud Sync stores notes and agent conversations in Neon while raw audio and standalone transcriptions do not sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles bot-free capture across desktop platforms, but its meeting sharing, sync and richer workflows partly depend on a cloud account or paid features and are less focused than Jamie.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is straightforward, but meeting capture needs microphone/accessibility and sometimes system-audio permissions plus model downloads; cloud processing, sharing and sync require an account or provider key and some meeting features are paid

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Jamie is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Jamie, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + whisper.cpp + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private bot-free meeting notes pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: calendar and CRM integrations; cross-call team analytics; recording recovery, mastering, hosting, and distribution.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
